keyEvents.impact: Opened two decades of coups culminating in Ba'athist one-party rule

keyEvents.event: Saddam Hussein invades Iran, starting an eight-year war
keyEvents.impact: Hundreds of thousands dead and a ruinous debt that pushed Baghdad toward Kuwait

keyEvents.event: Invasion of Kuwait and the 1991 Gulf War
keyEvents.impact: Crushing defeat, a decade of sanctions, and Kurdish self-rule under Western air cover
De-Ba'athification and sectarian power-sharing empowered Shia parties and opened the door to Iranian influence

keyEvents.event: ISIS captures Mosul; Sistani's fatwa births the Popular Mobilization Forces
keyEvents.impact: State near-collapse; Iran-aligned militias became a permanent armed power alongside the army

keyEvents.event: Defeat of ISIS and failed Kurdish independence referendum
keyEvents.impact: Baghdad retook Kirkuk; the federal-Kurdish balance tilted back to the center

keyEvents.event: Tishreen protest movement brings down the government
keyEvents.impact: Hundreds of protesters killed; deep youth alienation from the muhasasa sectarian system

keyEvents.event: Militia drone strikes on US forces after the Gaza war; US agrees to wind down the coalition mission
keyEvents.impact: Iraq became a battleground in the US-Iran confrontation it desperately wants to avoid

keyEvents.event: Ali al-Zaidi becomes prime minister after the November 2025 election; PMF factions fight alongside Iran in the 2026 war
keyEvents.impact: A new government under heavy US pressure to disarm Iran-aligned militias while Gulf states strike them

history.narrative: An oil-rich, fractured federal democracy squeezed between Washington and Tehran, with an army that shares the battlefield with Iran-aligned militias. Its governments survive by balancing Shia, Sunni and Kurdish factions and by keeping foreign wars from being fought on Iraqi soil.

redLines.description: Kurdish secession or foreign-backed partition of Iraq
Large-scale Turkish ground occupation in the Kurdistan Region beyond counter-PKK operations
US seizure of Iraqi oil revenues held at the New York Fed or secondary sanctions on Iraqi oil

internalDivisions.name: Shia-Sunni sectarian divide and the legacy of the ISIS war
Kurdistan Region autonomy, oil revenues and disputed Kirkuk
Iran-aligned militias versus state monopoly on arms

goals.description: Keep Iraq out of the US-Iran war and stop foreign strikes on its territory
Establish a state monopoly on arms by absorbing or disarming the PMF militias
Protect oil export revenue and diversify routes away from Hormuz via Turkey and the Gulf
Prevent an ISIS resurgence along the Syrian border
